abbQuestion: How do PVC / volume I/O patterns link to pod restarts?

expectFindings.why: node /proc/pressure/io some-stall crosses the 0.10 default bar while the historian fsyncs a telemetry burst; required per-device disk-IO + PVC volume-stats members are honestly unobservable on this emptyDir rig (every gap named on the finding).

On a bare rig WITHOUT node-exporter (default k3s box: ingest shows node-exporter:0) this phenomenon is honestly UNOBSERVABLE — Vigil stays silent rather than inventing it. Deploy node-exporter to surface it.

expectFindings.why: the scada-reader liveness probe (httpGet :9090/healthz, failureThreshold 3) trips while its read loop is wedged on the historian's cold disk scan; VALIDATED LIVE 2026-06-20: restartCount climbs 0->6+, lastState.terminated reason=Error exitCode=137 via 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP 503' (not OOM, not connection-refused).
expectFindings.observabilityDependency: the phenomenon's required members include probe-failure / failureThreshold / sustained signals the kubelet does NOT expose as metrics; only the restart counter (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, via --ksm-enabled) is observable, so on this rig it sits below its firing completeness. The restart is REAL and verifiable in pod status; Vigil does not surface the phenomenon from KSM's counter alone.

expectFindings.why: VALIDATED LIVE 2026-06-20: the scada-reader's busy connect/recv/timeout loop hits its 100m CPU limit and throttles; Vigil raises PHEN_THROTTLING_CASCADE on the scada-reader Container (completeness 0.5, the unobserved member named). This is the one genuinely-observable signal on the bare rig — and Vigil keeps it keyed to that single entity.

Vigil must NOT mint a cascade / causal edge linking the historian disk saturation to the SCADA restart. The two findings are a CO-OCCURRENCE, surfaced ADJACENTLY, each independently MEASURED and labelled.
mustNotFabricate.charter: Co-occurrence -> causal claim is rejected. A cascade is only an AUTHORED trigger->downstream edge lighting up; absent that edge, no cascade exists.

mustNotFabricate.statement: The unobservable storage members (per-device disk IO, kubelet_volume_stats PVC fill) must be reported as honest coverage gaps, NOT back-filled with an invented or learned threshold.

The scada-reader genuinely exhibits BOTH a CPU throttle (PHEN_THROTTLING_CASCADE, observed) and a liveness restart (real, from the disk stall). Vigil must NOT relate them — the throttle did not cause the restart (the restart is from the recv stall on the historian's cold read), and there is no authored edge between them. CONFIRMED LIVE: the throttle finding is keyed to the one Container entity and carries no cross-finding causal claim.
mustNotFabricate.charter: Co-occurrence -> causal claim is rejected. Two real phenomena on the same entity are still a co-occurrence, not a proven cause.
